## Why This Is Asked
Tests KV v2 basics, policy creation, and Kubernetes auth binding in a beginner scenario, plus practical read/rotate/revoke steps.

## Key Concepts
- KV v2 mounting and versioned secrets
- Policy syntax for read/list on a path
- Kubernetes auth role binding to a service account
- Token TTLs and lease-based rotation

## Code Example
```bash
vault secrets enable -path=tenant-abc kv-v2
vault policy write tenant-abc-read - <<'EOF'
path "secret/tenant-abc/config" { capabilities = ["read","list"] }
EOF
vault write auth/kubernetes/role/tenant-abc-role bound_service_account_names=tenant-abc-sa bound_namespace=ns/tenant-abc ttl=15m policies=tenant-abc-read
vault kv get secret/tenant-abc/config
vault kv patch secret/tenant-abc/config data=mykey=newvalue
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you automate rotation of a secret value and revoke all leases at offboarding?
- How would audit logs verify that only ns/tenant-abc-sa accessed tenant-abc/config?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests knowledge of per-tenant PKI in Vault, with namespace scoping, AppRole bindings, TTL governance, and safe disable/revocation workflows. It emphasizes accurate path usage, lease handling, and canary validation.

## Key Concepts
- Vault PKI per tenant in namespaces
- Role and domain constraints with TTL controls
- AppRole-bound policies for least privilege
- Lease revocation and CA rotation safety
- Canary testing for certificate issuance and revocation

## Code Example
```javascript
// Pseudo commands illustrating the flow (shell-style)
vault mount -t pki -path pki/tenant-<id> 
vault write pki/tenant-<id>/roles/tenant-<id>-tls allowed_domains="tenant-<id>.example.com" ttl="15m" max_ttl="1h" 
vault write auth/approle/role/tenant-<id>-login token_ttl=1h token_max_ttl=4h 
vault write pki/issue/tenant-<id>-tls common_name=host.tenant-<id>.example.com ttl=15m
```

## Follow-up Questions
